UPDATE: Tractor Tannie

By: Laura Byrne | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We catch up with Marconette and her mom to hear how the Tug of War world champs went.

Unique Selling Point:
After the success of Corne Els's fundraising tractor journey, and our story sharing her experience, we check in with Marconette and Corne to hear how the SA tug of war team fared in Switzerland, and what is next for this remarkable family.

Summary:
Marconette's team came 4th in the world champs - they tied 3rd place with the Basque Country but lost on points because their team weighed 400g more.
Marconette is planning to complete the current junior season, which ends in March 2024, and then take some time out from tug of war to focus on completing Matric. She has been selected as a prefect.

Press Release:


A heartwarming story of determination, community support, and the triumph of dreams. We revisit the epic journey of a mother, her daughter’s big dream – and the family’s ancient tractor that saved the day. In June Corne Els drove her family’s old Massey Ferguson nearly 1500km from Joburg to the Cape Winelands, raising R30,000 from supportive South Africans along the way to send Marconette to the Tug of War World Championships in Switzerland. Now, the travels and the competition behind her, Marconette reflects on the whirlwind of the last few months and how their under-23 tug of war team tied with the Basque Country in points and penalties but lost out on the bronze medal pull-offs due to a slight 400g weight disadvantage, settling for 5th place. Since communities along the way come out in force to support the quirky venture, we bring the happy update.

Script:


UPSOUND: CORNE ELSE [CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE] Hulle sê mos, ‘n boer maak ‘n plan en ‘n mamma maak twee, né?
VOICEOVER: It was a road trip like no other. For two weeks in June, Corné Else drove her family’s ancient Massey Ferguson tractor nearly 1500km from Krugersdorp to the Cape Winelands.
UPSOUND: CORNE ELSE [CORNE'S VIDEO DIARY] Hallo Marconette! Ons is reg om te ry, my bokkie. En hiermee gaan ons jou in Switzerland kry.
VOICEOVER: Her aim: to raise R30 000 to send her daughter, Marconette, to the world championships in tug of war.
UPSOUND: MARCONETTE [CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE] Ever since I was a young girl, I knew I wanted to be a Springbok in some sport. When tug of war came, I was like ok, this I can do. This will make me a Springbok.
VOICEOVER: As soon as Corné started up her trekker, her journey captured the imaginations of South Africans…who turned out their pockets. And in August, Marconette stepped onto the field in Switzerland.
UPSOUND: MARCONETTE ELSE: I couldn't sleep at all the night before. I think it was the excitement and the adrenaline pumping. So we talked until like 1:00 in the morning and then we were like, We have to sleep now! I thought we were good. But when you go to like I want to say world class athletes, you realize, Wow, I actually have a lot to learn and I can grow a lot still. So it was really a big experience for me.
VOICEOVER: Marconette’s Under 23 team tied for 4th place with the Basque Country. With points and penalties equal, the lighter team would go through to the bronze medal pull-offs. The South Africans weighed a mere 400g more, so they were relegated to 5th place.
UPSOUND: CORNE ELSE: We are very, very proud of, of what she achieved and and what the team accomplished.
VOICEOVER: For Corné, her “little South African adventure” continues to resonate.
UPSOUND: CORNE ELSE: I can't stop saying thank you to to to everybody that help us to to achieve this. I made so many good friends on, on this journey. I'm almost every day in contact with some of them. It's lekker. It became part of the life now. It's, the trekker story is, it's part of our life.
VOICEOVER: And life has some big milestones in store. Marconette has been selected as deputy head girl of her school next year. She’s got big dreams of travelling and starting her own business.
UPSOUND: MARCONETTE ELSE: Literally in the weeks leading up to the world champions, I was like, Why am I doing this sport? I'm not good enough. But when you actually go and compete, it's like a reassurance of, you worked hard, and you accomplished what you dreamed and what you worked for.
VOICEOVER: Of course, tug of war is part of the plan: Marconette hopes to compete in Germany next year…does that mean Corné will be taking another ride on the tractor??
UPSOUND: MARCONETTE ELSE: [laughs] Yeah, hopefully! If we can find another one.
